1) For hosted API customers (not Private) — do you retain raw prompt text anywhere beyond the request-processing pipeline? If yes, is it encrypted at rest and for how long?
2) Do you ever store generated outputs (completions)? If so, under what conditions (e.g., debugging, quality monitoring) and what's the retention?

Hi Ava — Marissa on security/compliance here, thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise, procurement-ready statement you can paste into your MAPPQ; I also added a few implementation notes and next steps.

Redwood Inference — formal summary (hosted API defaults):
- Prompt/request payloads: transiently handled in the runtime for inference. By default, we persist request logs (request metadata, request body) for 30 days to support debugging, abuse detection, and billing reconciliation. All persisted data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Generated outputs (completions): not persisted indefinitely by default. Outputs are stored for up to 30 days alongside request logs for short-term debugging and quality triage. Customers can opt out of server-side output retention at account-level (no retention) via the Console or API flag (store_outputs=false).
- Embeddings: not stored by default for hosted API requests unless the customer explicitly enables embedding storage. When stored, embeddings are pseudonymized and stored as vectors that are not reversible to original plaintext; they are logically linked to an internal identifier and retained for 365 days by default if enabled.
- Audit logs & admin access: Audit traces (route/model metrics, API access logs) are retained for 90 days by default. Access is restricted to RBAC roles (Engineering SRE, Support with restricted scopes, Security) with audit trails. Customers can request a data export (standard CSV/JSON) or initiate a purge via support ticket for hosted accounts.
- Deletion SLA: For hosted accounts, explicit deletion requests for persisted request logs and outputs are processed within 48 hours from ticket confirmation and completed from live systems within 7 days. Removal from periodic backups may take up to 30 days. For stricter SLAs or immediate removal, customers should consider Redwood Private (VPC) where data control and customer-managed storage apply.
- Data residency: Hosted accounts provisioned in the US are served from our us-east-1 region by default. Backups and disaster recovery replicas are kept within US-based regions; no replication to other geopolitical regions occurs for accounts that specify US residency. Private deployments can be provisioned inside customer VPCs or on-prem and follow customer-managed residency.

Implementation notes / limitations:
- If you require zero retention for both inputs and outputs, enable the account-level store_outputs=false and request that embedding storage remain disabled. Note that certain debugging support may be limited without request logs.
- We support field-level redaction on the client side and have SDK helpers to remove/replace PHI before sending.
- SOC 2: Our SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; I’ve attached a short data-retention summary for procurement (redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf).

Next steps:
1) Mina: I can add the above text into the MAPPQ and return the completed PDF in the next email.
2) Ava/Procurement: confirm if the deletion SLA (48h processing / 7d live removal / 30d backup window) is acceptable or if you require Private deployment options.
3) If needed, we can schedule a 20-min tech call to walk through SDK redaction patterns and the API flag to disable server-side output retention.

Ben will follow with the econ/pricing note for dedicated Private options if procurement wants a quote.

Regards,
